properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham.

  • Minor flooding is possible at Barham.
  • The Murray River at Barham is currently at 5.37 metres and rising, below the minor flood level.
  • It may exceed the minor flood level (5.50 metres) from overnight Thursday into Friday.
  • Further rises are possible as upstream flows arrive next week.
  • This Advice message replaces the Advice message issued at 4:02pm Tuesday 18 August.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings. 
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.

properties.name: Watch & Act
properties.webBody:
This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for the Loddon River upstream of Laanecoorie.

  • Moderate flooding is occurring at Bet Bet, with minor flooding occurring at Newstead.
  • 38.4mm of rain has fallen at Bet Bet in the 48 hours to 8:00am on Thursday.
  • At 8am on Thursday 20 August, the Bet Bet Creek at Bet Bet was at 5.36 metres, above the moderate flood level (5.00 metres).
  • At 8am on Thursday 20 August, the Loddon River at Newstead was at 3.05 metres, above the minor flood level (3.00 metres).
Stay safe - avoid the flooded area. Be aware of potential hazards caused by flooding and never enter floodwater.
What you should do:
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
  • If you are camping close to a creek or river, you may be at risk of flooding and need to move to higher ground, away from waterways.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
If you choose to leave:
  • Remember to take your pets, mobile phone, spare clothes and medications.
  • Travel to the home of family or friends who are in a safe location, away from flooding.
  • Turn off gas and electricity at your home or workplace.
  • Be aware of any road closures when you leave.
If you are travelling:
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around a find a safe alternative route.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
If you stay or if it is unsafe to leave:
  • Make sure you have enough food, drinking water, medications and pet food to survive for three to five days in case you become isolated.
  • Use plugs, sandbags or household items to block toilets, sinks and drains to stop sewerage backflow.
  • Lift it - move valuables and vital household items up on high surfaces, such as on top of tables, chairs, benches and beds.
Impacts in your area:
  • Be aware of water over roads. Do not drive, walk or play in floodwater.
  • Check the VicTraffic website (www.traffic.transport.vic.gov.au) for road closures and follow instructions from emergency services.
  • Stagnant water can be harmful to your health. Don’t swim, drink or wash in stagnant water.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 20/08/2026 01:00 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app
  • Facebook
  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.
Accessibility:

  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.

properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for Loddon River, Loddon Weir to Kerang.

  • Minor flooding is occurring at Appin South.
  • As of 12pm Wednesday, the Loddon River at Appin South is peaking at around 3.05 metres (above the minor flood level of 2.8 metres).
  • The Loddon River at Appin South is likely to remain above the minor flood level for the next few days.
  • 33.8mm of rain has fallen at Bet Bet and 20.8mm has fallen at Laanecoorie Reservoir overnight Tuesday and during Wednesday.
  • These totals have led to renewed river rises, but flood levels at Loddon Weir are not currently expected to go above the Minor level.
  • This Advice message replaces the Advice message issued at 1:13pm Tuesday 18 August.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Farmers should consider moving livestock and machinery to higher ground.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
Impacts in your area: 
  • Over-floor flooding of homes and buildings is not currently expected.
  • Lower areas of the Loddon floodplain may be flooded, including some minor roads.
  • Roads and bridges may be closed due to flooding.
  • Boating in floodwaters is dangerous due to debris, submerged trees and other hidden dangers.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.
